showcase.name: Desert Willow

risk.objective: mean revenue - lambda * CVaR_alpha(loss), over the equally weighted scenarios

instrument.settlement: clip(mean of the four first-published real-time 15-minute hub SPPs of the hour, floor, ceiling)
instrument.collateral: seller: (ceiling - entry) x contracts; buyer: (entry - floor) x contracts
instrument.entry_rule: assumed at fair value: the scenario-weighted mean of the hour's clipped settlement price, rounded to the nearest tick (half up)

forecast.method: day-type persistence: weighted mean of the newest day-ahead hub prices on file for days of the same type (weekday, or weekend and NERC holiday), weights newest first; a day counts only if it is at least `lag_days` before the target, the same lag the plan itself faces
forecast.node_rule: hub forecast plus the hourly node-minus-hub day-ahead basis averaged over the basis days

showcase.selection_rule: the solved arm with the highest objective_uusd; a tie goes to the earlier arm (A, B, C)

A.method: unhedged: schedule maximizing expected revenue (MILP, one binary per hour keeps charge and discharge apart)

B.method: overlay: arm A's schedule kept; hedge chosen to maximize mean - lambda * CVaR (LP)

C.method: joint: schedule and hedge chosen together to maximize mean - lambda * CVaR (MILP)

scenarios.method: each history day's day-ahead and real-time hub errors against the forecast rule, added to the target's hub forecast, crossed with each basis day's node-minus-hub day-ahead basis; equally weighted, no random numbers
scenarios.index_rule: scenario k pairs history_days[floor(k / 7)] with basis_days[k % 7]
scenarios.path_note: the hub path depends on the history day only (7 scenarios share each); the node path also carries the basis day
scenarios.hub_sum4_note: four times the hour's hedge settlement price at HB_NORTH, clipped to 0..40000; divide by 4 for cents per MWh

game.what: Desert Willow, operating day 2026-11-26: each arm's modeled day total under each of the 301 equally weighted scenarios, and its per-hour parts, from @gatelock/engine's revenueUusd
game.units: integer micro-USD (1 uusd = $0.000001); hours are CT hour-starting 0..23 of the operating day

parts.physical_uusd: per scenario and hour: (discharge kWh - charge kWh) x node day-ahead price (cents/MWh) x 10
parts.wear_uusd: per hour, every scenario alike: - discharge kWh x wear (200 cents/MWh) x 10
parts.hedge_uusd: per scenario and hour: contracts x (4 x entry - hub_sum4) x 2,500, i.e. contracts x (entry - settlement) per MWh; positive contracts sell
parts.fee_uusd: per hour, every scenario alike: - |contracts| x 35 cents x 10,000
parts.total_uusd: sum over hours of the four parts; equals revenueUusd for the full schedule and hedge, checked for every scenario

objective.form: objective = floor((mean x 1e6 - lambda_ppm x CVaR) / 1e6), mean = floor(sum of totals / 301), CVaR = mean loss over the worst 10% of scenarios (30.1 scenario weights: 30 whole, the 31st at 0.1), floored
objective.loss: loss = - total; a negative CVaR means even the worst tenth of scenarios averages a gain
objective.selection: the solved arm with the highest objective_uusd; a tie goes to the earlier arm (A, B, C)

limits.soc_rule: soc_h = soc_(h-1) + 0.85 x charge_kWh_h - discharge_kWh_h, starting from soc_open; kW over one hour is kWh
limits.lp_soc_margin_note: the optimizer keeps this margin inside the SOC limits; the accounting checks the declared limits

hedge.entry_rule: assumed at fair value: the scenario-weighted mean of the hour's clipped settlement price, rounded to the nearest tick (half up)
hedge.settlement: clip(mean of the four first-published real-time 15-minute hub SPPs of the hour, floor, ceiling)
hedge.hedge_cap_rule: an hour's sold contracts x 1 MWh may not exceed that hour's scheduled discharge; bought contracts may not exceed its scheduled charge
hedge.collateral_rule: seller: (ceiling - entry) x contracts; buyer: (entry - floor) x contracts
hedge.scope: published contract terms; the entry is the model's fair value, so the hedge is a scenario comparison, never an executed trade

game.scoring_a_new_plan: build {chargeKw[24], dischargeKw[24]} in whole kW and contracts[24] (positive sells), check the limits above, then total_k = sum_h [ (d_h - c_h) x node_cents[k][h] x 10 - d_h x 200 x 10 + q_h x (4 x entry_h - hub_sum4[k][h]) x 2500 - |q_h| x 350000 ] for each scenario k, and combine with the objective form; integer arithmetic reproduces the engine exactly

tail.note: worst totals first; ties broken by lower scenario index (the CVaR value does not depend on the tie-break)

page.title: DSWL_ESS_ESR1
page.body:
# DSWL_ESS_ESR1

## Asset and shadow plans
- DSWL_ESS_ESR1 is a real ERCOT battery asset. Its record contains shadow plans for operating day 2026-11-26.
- The public record does not establish actual operation of the plant.

## Shadow-plan verification
Keep these as distinct checks:
- Commitment verification.
- Input identification.
- Model constraints.
- Result reproduction.

## Reviewed rule
- Hedge entry is assumed to occur at model fair value.
- The result is a scenario comparison, not executable trading profit.
- Preserve the rule’s source, version, and time.

## Later reviews
- Label the assumed entry beside the result.
- Require an observed executable quote before making a trading-profit claim.

before.explanation: The available memory does not support an entry classification; request a cited review.

after.explanation: The reviewed memory classifies the model fair-value entry as an assumed scenario comparison. Keep that assumption beside the result; an executable quote is required for a trading-profit claim.

pages.title: Wattness Terminal
pages.summary: The Wattness Terminal at wattness.tech has six layers. Its public architecture comprises 18 parts, 48 connections, and 22 registered sections, including two sources, three selections, and one Ness routing component.
pages.body:
## Overview

The Wattness Terminal at wattness.tech is built in six layers. Its public architecture has 18 parts, 48 connections, and 22 registered sections.

The layers connect as follows: a source supplies a data reader; a data reader projects sections into a tab; a selection controls what a tab shows; a workspace contains or watches tabs; and Ness routes a question to a workspace.

## Sources layer (1 of 6)

The Terminal has two source parts:

- [[wattness-terminal-fleet-reference|Fleet reference]] supplies the Battery Page Reader, Fleet Board Reader, Month Close Reader, Fleet Map Reader, and QSEs Reader.
- [[wattness-terminal-mapped-locations|Mapped locations]] supplies the Battery Page Reader, Fleet Board Reader, Fleet Map Reader, Month Close Reader, and QSEs Reader. Its location and layer inputs retain mapping coverage and precision.

## Data readers layer (2 of 6)

- Month Close Reader is part of this layer.

## Selections layer (3 of 6)

The Terminal has three selections: Shared Fleet view, Battery focus, and Pane display settings.

## Tabs and sections layer (4 of 6)

- Month Close is part of this layer.

## Workspaces layer (5 of 6)

- [[wattness-terminal-fleet|Fleet]] and [[wattness-terminal-my-battery|My Battery]] are workspaces.

## Ness routing layer (6 of 6)

- The Terminal has one Ness routing component: Local workspace guide.

pages.title: Wattness Terminal Shared Fleet View
pages.summary: The Shared Fleet view shares metric, window, filters, circle, peers, and comparison settings between readers that declare them. It controls the Battery Page, Fleet Board, and Fleet Map, which are three of the Wattness Terminal’s five tabs and sections.
pages.body:
# Wattness Terminal Shared Fleet View

## Shared settings

The following settings are shared between readers that declare them:

- Metric
- Window
- Filters
- Circle
- Peers
- Comparison

## Connected views

The Shared Fleet view controls what is shown in:

- [[battery-page]]
- [[fleet-board]]
- [[fleet-map]]

These are three of the Wattness Terminal’s five tabs and sections. The other two are [[qses]] and [[month-close]].

pages.title: Wattness Terminal Battery Page
pages.summary: The Battery Page is part of layer 4 of 6 in Wattness Terminal and belongs to and is watched by both of its workspaces: My Battery and Fleet.
pages.body:
# Wattness Terminal Battery Page

- Part of the Tabs and sections layer (layer 4 of 6) in [[wattness-terminal]].
- [[wattness-terminal]] has two workspaces: [[my-battery]] and [[fleet]].
- The Battery Page belongs to and is watched by both workspaces.

pages.title: Month Close
pages.summary: Month Close is a registered section of the Wattness Terminal Month Close Reader. It belongs to the Fleet and My Battery workspaces, both of which watch its sections, and is controlled by Shared Fleet View and Pane Display Settings.
pages.body:
# Month Close

- Month Close is one of two registered sections of the [[wattness-terminal-month-close-reader]]; the other is Every month.
- The reader projects its sections into Month Close.

## Workspaces and controls

- Month Close belongs to the [[fleet]] and [[my-battery]] workspaces.
- Both Fleet and My Battery watch sections of Month Close.
- Month Close is controlled by [[shared-fleet-view]] and [[pane-display-settings]].

pages.title: QSEs
pages.summary: QSEs is a tab in the Fleet workspace and belongs to both Fleet and My Battery. Both workspaces watch its registered sections; Pane display settings and Shared Fleet view control it.
pages.body:
# QSEs

## Registered sections
- Every QSE
- QSE
- Switches in and out

## Workspace connections
- [[fleet]] contains a QSEs tab and watches sections of QSEs.
- QSEs also belongs to [[my-battery]], which watches sections of QSEs.

## Controls
- [[pane-display-settings]] controls QSEs.
- [[shared-fleet-view]] controls QSEs.

pages.summary: My Battery is a workspace with Battery Page and QSEs tabs that watches sections of Battery Page and Fleet Board.
pages.body:

- [[qses|QSEs]]

## Watched sections
- [[battery-page|Battery Page]]

pages.title: Wattness Terminal Fleet
pages.summary: Fleet helps identify batteries trailing their neighbors and investigate the performance gap. It watches sections of Fleet Board and Battery Page.
pages.body:
# Wattness Terminal Fleet

Fleet is intended to show which batteries trail their neighbors and what is behind the performance gap.

## Watched sections

- Sections of [[fleet-board]]
- Sections of [[battery-page]]

pages.title: Fleet Board Reader
pages.summary: A layer 2 Data readers component of Wattness Terminal that draws on Fleet reference and Mapped locations to project eight sections into Fleet Board, which is in the Tabs and sections layer (layer 4 of 6).
pages.body:
# Fleet Board Reader

## Role and data sources
- Part of the Data readers layer (layer 2 of 6) in Wattness Terminal.
- Gets data from Fleet reference and Mapped locations.
- Projects its sections into Fleet Board, which is part of the Wattness Terminal Tabs and sections layer (layer 4 of 6). Shared section projections retain source scope, missing observations, and Figure/Table identities.

## Registered sections
1. Fleet at a glance
2. Fleet revenue
3. Where the revenue comes from
4. All batteries ranked
5. Batteries on the map
6. Fleet heat map
7. Check your battery
8. Method and sources

pages.title: Pane Display Settings
pages.summary: Per-pane display settings control what appears in the Battery Page, Fleet Board, Fleet Map, Month Close, and QSEs, and remain with saved arrangements.
pages.body:
# Pane Display Settings

- Control what is shown in [[battery-page]], [[fleet-board]], [[fleet-map]], [[month-close]], and [[qses]]. The Fleet Board is controlled by these pane display settings.
- Per-pane display settings remain with [[saved-arrangements]].

pages.title: Fleet Board
pages.summary: The Fleet Board belongs to the Fleet workspace, is controlled by Shared Fleet view, and is watched by both the My Battery and Fleet workspaces.

pages.title: QSEs Reader
pages.summary: A layer 2 Data readers component of the Wattness Terminal that reads Fleet reference and Mapped locations, registers three sections, and projects them into QSEs in the Tabs and sections layer (layer 4 of 6), preserving source context and Figure/Table identities.
pages.body:
# QSEs Reader

The QSEs Reader is part of the [[wattness-terminal]]’s Data readers layer (layer 2 of 6). It projects content into [[qses]], which is part of the Wattness Terminal’s Tabs and sections layer (layer 4 of 6).

## Data sources

- Fleet reference
- Mapped locations

## Registered sections

- Every QSE
- QSE
- Switches in and out

The reader projects these sections into QSEs. Its shared section projections retain source scope, missing observations, and Figure/Table identities.

pages.title: Cached Disclosure
pages.summary: Cached disclosure is one of the areas covered by the Wattness Terminal Fleet reference.
pages.body:
# Cached Disclosure

- Cached disclosure is covered by the Wattness Terminal Fleet reference, alongside daily and monthly records, joins, and coverage guards.

pages.title: Battery Page Reader
pages.summary: Layer 2 data reader in the Wattness Terminal that projects seven registered sections from Fleet reference and Mapped locations into Battery Page while retaining source scope, missing observations, and Figure/Table identities.
pages.body:
# Battery Page Reader

The Battery Page Reader is part of the [[wattness-terminal]] Data readers layer (layer 2 of 6). It gets data from [[fleet-reference]] and [[mapped-locations]] and projects its sections into [[battery-page]].

## Registered sections

1. In plain words
2. Ranks and peers
3. Where the gap comes from
4. By month
5. Daily yield against peers
6. Head-to-head
7. Spread and capture

Its shared section projections retain source scope, missing observations, and Figure/Table identities.

pages.summary: Battery focus is the current battery pick. It controls what appears in Fleet Board and Fleet Map; a Battery Page can follow it or retain its own battery.

Battery focus represents the current battery pick.

## Where It Applies

- **[[battery-page]]:** Can follow battery focus or retain its own battery.
- **[[fleet-board]]:** Battery focus controls what is shown.
- **[[fleet-map]]:** Battery focus controls what is shown.
